en.headline: Fire Services expands IoT fire alarm scheme to another 6000 old buildings
en.dek: More than 300 buildings have expressed interest so far, but none have completed installation yet as owners negotiate costs and consensus.
body: The Fire Services Department will expand its Internet of Things smart fire alarm scheme this month to buildings of seven storeys or above, covering around 6,000 additional old blocks, acting deputy chief fire officer Lai Kin-mo said.

The scheme, previously approved for about 3,600 buildings of six storeys or below, allows owners to install wireless detectors that alert the department within seconds of detecting smoke or carbon monoxide, as an alternative to traditional hose reels and manual alarms. Installation can take two to four weeks instead of one to two years, and costs can fall by up to about 60 per cent.

Lai said more than 300 buildings had submitted expressions of interest, which the department described as ideal, but none had finished installation. Owners often need time to reach consensus at meetings and to agree on service-provider plans and fees. The department also plans to accept a compromise sprinkler design for about 900 buildings that face space constraints.

zh.headline: 消防處將物聯網火警偵測系統擴展至約6000幢7層或以上舊樓
zh.dek: 至今逾300幢樓宇提交意向書，反應理想，但暫時未有大廈完成安裝，業主需時達共識及商討工程費用。
body: 消防處署理副消防總長黎健武表示，處方將於本月內發通函，把物聯網火警偵測系統作為遵辦消防安全指示的替代方案，擴展至7層或以上目標樓宇，預計涵蓋約6000幢大廈。
系統早前已適用於約3600幢6層或以下樓宇，可自動偵測火警並將訊號直接傳送至消防通訊中心，工程不受結構與空間限制，時間可由1至2年縮短至2至4周，費用最多可減約六成。
黎健武指，至今已接獲逾300份意向書，反應理想，但暫時未有大廈完成安裝，主要因為業主需要較長時間召開大會達成共識，以及商討不同服務提供者的計劃與費用。處方亦計劃接納折衷式花灑系統，適用於約900幢空間受限的樓宇。
